currentContext.business: Bhageria Industries manufactures dye intermediates and specialty chemicals — H-Acid, Gamma Acid, Vinyl Sulphone and, from December 2025, plasticizers — supplying textile, leather, paper, food-processing and pharmaceutical manufacturers in India and in more than ten export markets. Alongside that chemicals engine it runs a renewable-energy business entered in 2015, generating power from utility-scale and rooftop solar projects held through subsidiaries and sold under long-term power purchase agreements. A third and still-early pharmaceutical arm is being built around R&D in the Vitamins and Steroids API categories, and the AR is explicit that its contribution to results remains modest.

currentContext.strengths: Backward integration into its own raw material production — the AR states this keeps it insulated from external supply shocks and gives a cost advantage that competitors sourcing externally cannot match|Plants ran at 95-97% utilisation through much of FY 2025-26 on sustained Southeast Asian and European export demand|In-house research and development supporting product development, process improvement and environmental stewardship|Four-product specialty chemical portfolio (H-Acid, Gamma Acid, Vinyl Sulphone, Plasticizers) sold across six end-market industries, so the chemicals business is not dependent on any single industry|Export franchise spanning more than ten countries, with long-term customer relationships named as a driver of this year's volumes|Three-segment structure — chemicals, solar generation under long-term PPAs, and pharmaceuticals — with the solar arm built organically rather than by acquisition
currentContext.strategies: Grow by disciplined extension of existing specialty chemicals expertise rather than unrelated diversification — the H-Acid capacity expansion and the plasticizers entry are both framed as extensions of the same competence, not a pivot|Deepen R&D capability in both chemicals and pharmaceuticals|Bring more automation into manufacturing processes|Continue strengthening global customer relationships|Maintain financial discipline — explicitly refusing to chase growth at the expense of margin or balance-sheet health|Build the solar portfolio organically through patient project development and state-government relationships (MSKVY 2.0) rather than through acquisitions or heavy capital expenditure, monetised via long-term power purchase agreements|Build a longer-dated pharmaceutical position through R&D and regulatory infrastructure in the high-value Vitamins and Steroids API categories, with management explicitly cautioning that the timeline requires continued patience|Use solar generation both to earn dependable PPA-linked returns and to reduce the carbon footprint of the industries served|The Company presents governance itself as the source of its distribution record, stating that strong governance has helped it deliver wealth to shareholders in the form of uninterrupted dividends; declaring a dividend on equity shares is again put to members as ordinary business at the 37th AGM. All strategic decisions on investment and diversification, and major decisions on procurement, commercial matters and finance, are taken only after Board approval. The Company maintains a Board-level policy framework — including a Dividend Distribution Policy and a Policy for determining Material Subsidiaries — published on its website; under the latter it has no material subsidiary. The AR does not, in this bundle, state a target payout ratio, a buyback intent or a leverage policy.|Climate commitments anchored in TCFD, CDP and SBTi, with science-based targets stated to guide the Company's decarbonisation work|Emissions and effluent controls at the manufacturing footprint: advanced scrubbers, dust recovery systems and low-emission cooling technologies, described as holding the footprint in check even as output has grown|Own-generation decarbonisation: the Khanapur solar plant is operational and feeding clean power into the grid, and the solar business is framed as existing partly to reduce the carbon footprint of the industries the Company serves|Energy-efficiency programme: capacitor power banks, microturbines recovering waste energy, and the 'Smart Comm' digital energy management system|CSR spend of Rs 33.99 lakh in FY 2025-26 directed across five social sectors — healthcare (village medical centre offering free Ayurveda, Naturopathy and Homeopathy treatment, eye health camps and preventive screening for chronic conditions such as diabetes), education (scholarships, learning materials, school and library infrastructure), infrastructure, animal welfare and national heritage; the prose states healthcare received the largest share, followed by education. Per-sector amounts appear in the source as detached figures (Rs 12.94, 8.75, 4.80, 4.50 and 4.50 lakh) that cannot be matched to their labels in the extracted layout, so no sector-level amount is asserted here|Anti-Sexual Harassment Policy with a constituted Internal Complaints Committee; the Company affirms no complaints were received during FY 2025-26|Board-adopted Code of Conduct for Directors, Senior Management and employees, with compliance confirmed by all Board members and senior management|Cordial industrial relations across all locations, with stated commitments to employee well-being, workplace safety, diversity and equal opportunity|Disclosure note: BRSR ceased to apply to the Company from March 31, 2025 under Regulation 3(2A) of the SEBI Listing Regulations, so the FY26 Annual Report contains no separate Business Responsibility & Sustainability Reporting section — no assured, quantified ESG metric set (emissions, energy, water, waste intensity) is disclosed for FY26
currentContext.expansion: FY 2025-26 was an execution year across all three legs. In chemicals, the Company lifted H-Acid manufacturing capacity from 400 to 500 metric tons per month — a move it expects to contribute an incremental Rs 50-75 crore to annual revenue once fully ramped — and opened an entirely new product line at Tarapur, Maharashtra, with plasticizer production commencing in December 2025 and adding a fourth specialty chemical to a portfolio that had centred on H-Acid, Gamma Acid and Vinyl Sulphone. Management frames both as disciplined extensions of existing specialty-chemicals expertise rather than diversification, and notes plants ran at 95-97% utilisation through much of the year. In renewables, subsidiary Rahuri Cleantech Private Limited commissioned a 14 MW solar power plant during 2025-26 — a 7 MW plant at Pimpalgaon Wagha, Ahilyanagar in February 2026 and a further 7 MW at Bhatkudgaon, Maharashtra in March 2026 — followed by an additional 7 MW at Khanapur, Maharashtra in May 2026, taking total installed capacity to 21 MW. These plants are part of a larger 32 MW capacity build-out underway through the Maharashtra government's MSKVY 2.0 scheme; the Chairman stresses this was achieved through disciplined, organic project development rather than acquisitions or significant capital expenditure. In pharmaceuticals the Company continues to invest in R&D and regulatory/manufacturing infrastructure for the Vitamins and Steroids API categories, but is explicit that this is a longer-term journey whose contribution to results remains modest. The Company manufactures from Vapi, Gujarat and Tarapur, Maharashtra. The AR discloses no rupee capex quantum: the Note 48 'Capital Commitments' block reaches this bundle as a heading and a units line only, with no figure attached.

risks.risk: Supply chain risk (the AR's own first named risk)
risks.note: Disruptions in raw material availability, logistics constraints, supplier concentration, geopolitical developments and input cost fluctuations may impact production schedules and profitability. Mitigation cited: a diversified supplier base, long-term supplier relationships, inventory monitoring, strategic procurement planning and continuous evaluation of alternative sourcing.

risks.risk: Competition risk (the AR's own second named risk)
risks.note: Intense competition from domestic and international players may pressure market share, pricing and margins. Mitigation cited: product quality, customer relationships, operational efficiency, innovation, cost optimisation and market diversification.

The MD&A states profitability margins were impacted by fluctuations in input costs and competitive market conditions, and attributes the decline in operating profit margin to changes in product mix, competitive conditions and higher input costs — EBITDA margin moderated year on year on both a standalone and a consolidated basis even as revenue grew sharply. The global dye intermediates market is separately described as under margin pressure from movements in aromatic feedstocks such as Benzene and Naphthalene.

risks.risk: Freight, energy and logistics cost volatility plus geopolitical disruption of global trade
risks.note: The Group's performance is described as delivered amidst volatility in raw material prices, fluctuations in energy and freight costs and continued geopolitical uncertainties affecting global trade; shipping disruptions on key trade routes raised the overall cost of imports and exports.

A significant share of revenue is export-linked and the MD&A notes that currency fluctuations against the US Dollar created challenges for export-oriented businesses; weak European manufacturing activity and anti-dumping duties/trade restrictions imposed by several countries are also flagged.

risks.risk: Environmental, pollution and safety regulatory exposure
risks.note: The Secretarial Auditor records that apart from environment, pollution and safety related compliances there are no specific laws applicable to the Company, which locates the Company's principal regulatory burden in exactly that area; globally the MD&A notes stricter environmental regulation, carbon-related trade measures and buyer-enforced ZDHC/OEKO-TEX mandates down the chemical supply chain, and domestically that state-level pollution control protocols and CETP upgrades are raising the cost of participation.

risks.risk: Segment concentration in chemicals, with the pharma leg loss-making
risks.note: The Chemicals segment supplies the overwhelming majority of both revenue and EBIT, while the Pharma segment recorded negative EBIT in both FY26 and FY25 on standalone and consolidated bases and the Solar segment's revenue and EBIT were broadly flat year on year — so group earnings currently rest on a single segment's cycle.

risks.risk: Working-capital intensity of the dye intermediates industry
risks.note: The industry's working capital cycles are described as intensive, requiring disciplined credit management and efficient inventory control; the Company's receivables and inventory turnover improved this year, but the structural requirement remains.

one-line thesis: Bhageria Industries Limited is a specialty chemicals manufacturer facing challenges due to a voluntary closure notice from the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board, which may impact its credit profile. The company's credit rating has been revised to CARE A with a negative outlook. The company needs to address the pollution control issues to maintain its creditworthiness.

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).
